mapping.observation: The pilot made clarification, minimal planning, verification boundaries, and stop fields explicit, but did not prove comparative benefit or independent parallel/recovery mechanisms.
mapping.learning: Persist one execution-discipline envelope per admitted task; use a light branch for simple work and a structured branch for medium/complex work.
mapping.reality_scope: ACE task admission and existing TaskPool lifecycle
mapping.expected_result: Complex tasks expose a bounded pre-execution record and fail closed when its minimum goal, plan, or verification fields are malformed, without adding a second runtime.
mapping.verification_method: Focused deterministic regression, adjacent TaskPool/lifecycle regression, py_compile, diff integrity, and preservation of existing single-daemon and external-side-effect boundaries.
constraints: do not adopt mandatory full planning for simple work
refuse parallel execution by default for shared or dependent state
do not treat same-worker challenge passes as independent review
use the existing continue gate for recovery only
do not create a second scheduler, router, queue, or runtime

review_basis: the source artifact and adversarial review are hash-bound
the source outcome remains INCONCLUSIVE and no comparative speed or quality claim is promoted
the accepted implementation is additive, deterministic, and uses the existing TaskPool writer
unsupported parallelism, independent review, and recovery claims remain deferred or rejected
